MUSIC 127.name: Introduction to Music Technology
MUSIC 127.description: Introduction to music technology, for first-year students in B.A. Music Technology, B.F.A. Sound Design, and B.M. Music Composition.

MUSIC 177.name: ROARS Lab
MUSIC 177.description: Research of the Arts, Recording, and Sound lab. General catalog credit range is 1-3cr, max 9; the Music Technology B.M.'s own bulletin page states it is repeated once per semester across all four years for a cumulative 8cr, modeled here as one 1cr enrollment per semester.

MUSIC 437.name: Music Information Retrieval and Computer-Assisted Music
MUSIC 437.description: Music information retrieval and computer-assisted music. Bulletin recommends (not enforces) prior INART 50.

MUSIC 451.name: Computer Programming for Musicians
MUSIC 451.description: Music programming in environments like SuperCollider and Max/MSP. Bulletin credit max is 12 across repeated enrollments (also satisfiable via permission of program, not modeled).

MUSIC 452.description: Use of sound synthesis software for music creation. Bulletin's own prereq text cites 'INART 50Z', which could not be confirmed as a distinct course from INART 50 (the INART department listing has no separate 50Z entry) -- treated as INART 50.

MUSIC 453.name: Recording Studio Training
MUSIC 453.description: Operating a multi-track recording studio: mic theory, signal flow, mixing/mastering, maintenance.

MUSIC 423.name: Music Entrepreneurship
MUSIC 423.description: Entrepreneurship principles applied to the music profession.

MUSIC 431.name: Advanced Tonal Analysis
MUSIC 431.description: Advanced analysis of tonal music. Bulletin credit max is 6 across repeated enrollments.

MUSIC 433.name: Advanced Analysis of Twentieth-Century Music
MUSIC 433.description: Advanced analysis of twentieth-century music. Bulletin credit max is 6 across repeated enrollments.

MUSIC 438.name: The Business of Music
MUSIC 438.description: The business of music. Bulletin requires 5th-semester standing, which the planner schema does not model directly.

MUSIC 461W.name: Studies in Music History: Antiquity to 1600
MUSIC 461W.description: Studies in music history, antiquity to 1600. Bulletin credit max is 6 across repeated enrollments. Writing Across the Curriculum.

MUSIC 462W.name: Studies in Music History: 1550-1750
MUSIC 462W.description: Studies in music history, 1550-1750. Bulletin credit max is 6 across repeated enrollments. Writing Across the Curriculum.

MUSIC 463W.description: Studies in music history, 1700-1900. Bulletin credit max is 6 across repeated enrollments. Writing Across the Curriculum. Bulletin's own prereq cites MUSIC 261 (not 262, despite this course covering the later 1700-1900 period) -- verified verbatim, a real catalog quirk not a fetch error.

MUSIC 464W.name: Studies in Music History: 1850-Present
MUSIC 464W.description: Studies in music history, 1850 to present. Bulletin credit max is 6 across repeated enrollments. Writing Across the Curriculum.

MUSIC 114.description: Continuation of class voice instruction for B.F.A. Musical Theatre and Acting majors.

MUSIC 101.name: Music Common Hour
MUSIC 101.description: Weekly convocation covering topics relevant to the music profession.

MUSIC 122.name: Basic Musicianship II
MUSIC 122.description: Continuation of sight singing and dictation. Bulletin lists this as a mutual corequisite of MUSIC 132 -- modeled one-directional (MUSIC 122 requires MUSIC 132 concurrently, not vice versa) since the engine's same-term scheduling can't resolve a mutual two-way concurrent requirement; both are scheduled in the same semester regardless.

MUSIC 132.name: Music Theory II
MUSIC 132.description: Continuation of tonal music theory. Bulletin also lists this as a mutual corequisite of MUSIC 122 -- see MUSIC 122's note on why pairwise concurrency isn't modeled both directions.

MUSIC 162.name: Introduction to Music History
MUSIC 162.description: Introduction to the history of Western music.

MUSIC 222.name: Basic Musicianship IV
MUSIC 222.description: Continuation of intermediate sight singing and dictation.

MUSIC 261.name: Survey of Music History I
MUSIC 261.description: Survey of Western music history, part I.

MUSIC 262.name: Survey of Music History II
MUSIC 262.description: Survey of Western music history, part II.

MUSIC 270.description: Secondary chord progressions, transposition, improvisation, accompanying techniques, and score reading.

MUSIC 332.description: Analytical methods and compositional theories applied to twentieth-century music.

MUSIC 476W.description: Senior capstone project appropriate to the student's B.A. option (research paper, performance with program notes, or related paper). Bulletin requires 7th-semester standing, which the planner schema does not model directly. Writing Across the Curriculum.

MUSIC 154.description: Performance and teaching techniques on woodwind instruments for music education majors.

MUSIC 240.description: Introduction to the field of music education. Real gap: this course underlies MUSIC 295A/341/345/395A as a prereq, but the Music Education B.M.E. Suggested Academic Plan never names it directly -- it's the actual course behind that plan's generic 'Education elective' item in Year 1 Spring.

MUSIC 266.name: Basic Conducting
MUSIC 266.description: Foundational instruction and practical experience in conducting techniques.

MUSIC 295A.name: Early Field Experience in Music Education
MUSIC 295A.description: Early field experience for music education majors. Bulletin also requires 4th-semester standing, which the planner schema does not model directly.

MUSIC 341.description: Instructional materials for music education, restricted to students accepted into the Teacher Education Degree Program in Music.

MUSIC 444W.name: Emphasis in Elementary and Intermediate Band

MUSIC 445W.description: High school band emphasis, one of six freely-selectable Music Education emphasis options. Writing Across the Curriculum.

MUSIC 446W.description: Strings and orchestra emphasis, one of six freely-selectable Music Education emphasis options. Writing Across the Curriculum.
